chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar. He said: I said to Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq, peace be upon him:
By what is the saved one known? He said: Whoever's actions are congruent with his words is saved, and whoever's actions are not congruent with his words is surely put down.

key_terms.النَّاجِي: the saved one — one whose faith is genuine and stable
key_terms.مُسْتَوْدَعٌ: deposited/put down — one whose faith is temporary and may be withdrawn
key_terms.مُوَافِقًا: congruent — indicating alignment between action and speech

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq define who is truly saved?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq defines salvation through the alignment of deeds with words. Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar asks him how one recognizes the saved person. The Imam provides a concise criterion: genuine believers demonstrate their faith through consistency between what they say and what they do. Those whose actions contradict their speech are described as mustawda' (deposited), a term indicating temporary or unstable faith that may be withdrawn.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
